title: Medical Office Replacement Sourcing
name: Medical Office Replacement Sourcing
metaTitle: Medical Office Replacement Sourcing in San Jose, CA
metaDescription: 1031 medical office sourcing across San Jose's hospital-anchored corridors, from lease review to seismic exposure, coordinated ahead of the 45-day deadline.

sections.html: Medical office is the asset class San Jose investors tend to ask about last, usually after the 45-day clock is already running. That is backwards. A physician-group lease reads nothing like a retail or industrial lease, and the buildings sit in a handful of predictable clusters around the county's hospital campuses rather than spread evenly across the city. We source and screen medical office replacement property the way we have since before the Regional Medical Center's Alum Rock campus finished its last expansion.

sections.heading: Where the Medical Office Stock Actually Sits
sections.html:
San Jose's medical office buildings cluster tight around a few anchors: the O'Connor Hospital campus off The Alameda, Regional Medical Center of San Jose near Jackson Avenue and Alum Rock, and Kaiser Permanente's Cottle Road campus in the south of the city. A smaller pocket of physician-owned suites runs along Hedding Street and through the Willow Glen medical corridor near Willow Street and Lincoln Avenue. Buildings within a mile of one of these anchors hold occupancy through specialty-group turnover far better than stand-alone office-park buildings that happen to have a medical tenant today and a software tenant tomorrow.

That distinction matters for identification. A building marketed as medical office because a single urgent-care tenant signed a five-year lease is a different risk than a condo suite inside an established physician campus with three or four practices sharing common infrastructure.

sections.heading: Reading a Physician-Group Lease Before It Goes on the List
sections.html: We pull the rent roll and look past the headline rate to the structure underneath: is this a single-tenant net lease to a surgical group, or a multi-tenant condo with several practices on staggered terms? A specialty group's lease durability tracks its hospital privileges and its insurance-panel relationships more than its balance sheet, and those relationships can shift if a hospital system opens its own outpatient building nearby. We check whether the anchor tenant's referral base depends on proximity to one hospital or is portable across the county before recommending a property for the identification list.

sections.heading: Seismic and Title 24 Exposure on Older Buildings
sections.html: A meaningful share of the medical office stock near downtown and along Hedding Street predates current seismic standards, and unreinforced masonry retrofit obligations do not go away because a building changes hands through an exchange. Tenant-improvement permits for a new physician suite can also trigger Title 24 energy-compliance upgrades that were never required under the prior lease. We underwrite retrofit and compliance exposure into the replacement decision itself rather than leaving it for the buyer to discover after the 180-day exchange period closes.

sections.heading: What Has to Check Out Before a Building Makes the 45-Day List
sections.html:
Before we recommend a medical office property for identification, we confirm the following against the physical building and the lease file rather than relying on the marketing package alone:

  • Seismic retrofit status and any outstanding compliance orders on file with the city
  • ADA parking ratio measured against the actual patient volume the tenant mix generates
  • Remaining lease term set against the exchange buyer's loan amortization schedule
  • Ownership structure, since a condo interest carries different assignability rules than fee-simple title
  • Shared ingress and egress where multiple practices use one entrance and one loading area

None of that shows up in a one-page flyer, and all of it changes how a building performs once you own it.

sections.heading: Parking Ratios and Patient Flow Are Not the Same as Office Metrics
sections.html:
A standard office building's parking ratio assumes employees who park once and stay all day, while a medical office building sees a much higher turnover rate as patients arrive for appointments, park for an hour, and leave. A building that meets a typical office parking standard can still feel undersized once an urgent-care tenant or an imaging center moves in and patient volume spikes at predictable hours. We estimate patient turnover for the specific tenant mix, beyond a generic medical office assumption, before signing off on a property's parking adequacy.

Ambulatory surgery tenants add another layer, since they typically require recovery-room adjacency, wider corridors for gurneys, and a separate patient drop-off zone that a standard exam-room suite layout doesn't provide. A building can carry a medical office label on the listing sheet and still be poorly configured for the specific type of practice a buyer expects to lease it to, which is exactly the kind of mismatch we're screening for before a property reaches a client's identification list.

faqs.q: Does a medical office building qualify as like-kind to the property I'm selling?
faqs.a: Since the 2017 tax law narrowed 1031 to real property, essentially any real estate held for investment or business use is like-kind to any other, so a medical office building qualifies as like-kind to an apartment complex, a retail center, or raw land. The question is never eligibility; it's whether the tenant mix and building condition fit what you actually want to own.

faqs.q: How do you evaluate whether a physician group will renew?
faqs.a: We look at how portable the group's referral base is. A practice tied tightly to one hospital's privileges behaves differently than a group that treats patients across several Santa Clara County systems. We also check whether a competing outpatient building recently opened near the hospital the tenant depends on.

faqs.q: Can a medical office condo suite count as one of my three identified properties?
faqs.a: Yes, a condo interest in a medical building can be named under the three-property rule the same as a fee-simple parcel, provided the identification is specific enough to satisfy the 45-day requirement. We flag the ownership structure early so the assignability terms don't surprise anyone at closing.

faqs.q: What happens if a seismic retrofit isn't finished when the exchange closes?
faqs.a: The exchange can still close, but outstanding retrofit obligations transfer with the building and should be priced into the deal and disclosed in the purchase agreement. We surface retrofit status during sourcing specifically so it's negotiated before the 180-day exchange period runs out, not discovered afterward.

faqs.q: Do you tell me which property to buy?
faqs.a: No. We source, screen, and coordinate the physical and lease due diligence; your tax advisor and your qualified intermediary confirm the exchange structure and the deadlines. We don't give tax advice, and we recommend every client confirm treatment with their own advisor before identifying a property.
